nodes.label: Shared multi-tenant VPS (b2b + GradeSentinel behind one Caddy)
nodes.rationale: The box already runs GradeSentinel (grades.railtech.uz) and Caddy owning 80/443 — never stop Caddy, gradesentinel-* services, or the actions.runner service. RailTech runs in Docker bound to loopback only (so Docker's iptables cannot bypass ufw) and is published through the existing Caddy.

nodes.label: Caddy conf.d fragment pattern (per-project import)
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenant import pattern: the master /etc/caddy/Caddyfile (global block + import /etc/caddy/conf.d/*.caddy) is never touched by a project deploy — each project owns exactly one fragment in conf.d. This is what keeps a GradeSentinel deploy from clobbering b2b and vice-versa. The fragment must be re-applied by hand after every repo edit; this gap is exactly how the prod SPA lived for months without Cache-Control headers so returning users never saw shipped deploys (2026-08-05 incident).

nodes.label: Edge rate-limit via caddy-ratelimit custom binary (INF-01)
nodes.rationale: The b2b fragment uses the caddy-ratelimit module NOT in stock apt Caddy — a custom binary swapped via mv (cp fails 'text file busy') and apt-mark hold so upgrades never clobber it; security updates are therefore manual. Coarse per-IP ceilings: /api/v1/auth/* 30/min, /admin/* 60/min. DRF throttle stays the primary control; the edge layer matters most for /admin/*, which has no DRF throttle.

nodes.label: DB connection budget (per-process pools)
nodes.rationale: dj-db-conn-pool opens a SQLAlchemy pool PER PROCESS and the stack has ~9 pool-owning processes, so peak connections = 9 × (DB_POOL_SIZE + DB_MAX_OVERFLOW). The old 10+20 sizing gave a ~270 ceiling, exhausted the DB-VPS max_connections=100 and made the backup gate fail with 'connection slots are reserved for SUPERUSER' (2026-07-08 incident). New defaults 3+5 → ~72 ceiling; rule: 9 × (POOL_SIZE + MAX_OVERFLOW) + ~15 (backup/migrations/psql) < max_connections; all env-tunable without a code deploy.

nodes.label: Pre-deploy backups & restore procedure (INF-04)
nodes.rationale: Dumps land in /opt/railtech-b2b/backups/predeploy-<ts>.dump (rsync-excluded, 14 kept); the DB-VPS independently keeps a daily pg_dump cron. Restore (--clean --if-exists) drops data written after the dump — it is a disaster rollback, not an undo button; for surgical fixes prefer a reverse migration, and the CODE must be rolled back to the pre-migration commit too.

nodes.label: HTTP/3 QUIC requires UDP 443 open in firewall
nodes.rationale: Caddy advertises alt-svc h3=":443" and listens on UDP 443; if ufw allows only 443/tcp, browsers cache the alt-svc, retry over QUIC, get UDP silently dropped, stall on the QUIC timeout and fall back to TCP — the site 'opens on the tenth attempt'. Fix: ufw allow 443/udp, or disable HTTP/3 via a Caddy global block if the region blocks UDP 443.

nodes.label: Dedicated self-hosted GitHub runner (label railtech-b2b)
nodes.rationale: The GradeSentinel runner is repo-scoped and cannot run this repo's jobs, so a dedicated runner is registered under a 'deploy' user in the docker group owning /opt/railtech-b2b and /var/www/railtech-b2b.
